claims: The Artemis II mission is designed to last approximately 10 days.
The Artemis II mission has a four-person crew.
The Artemis II crew will journey around the Moon and return to Earth.
The Artemis II mission is launching on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission is a crewed flight.
The Artemis II mission will test Orion's systems.
The Artemis II mission has a planned splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
As of April 1, 2026, the Artemis II mission is approximately 5 hours 29 minutes into it.
The Artemis II mission goal is a crewed "free return" trajectory loop around the far side of the Moon and back.
The Artemis II mission reaches a maximum distance of over 250,000 miles from Earth.
The Artemis II mission will take around three to four days to reach the Moon.
The Artemis II mission will perform a lunar flyby.
The Artemis II mission will take another four days to return to Earth.
The Artemis I mission was uncrewed.
The Artemis I mission took place in 2022.
The Artemis I mission was a three-week mission.
The Artemis I mission was longer than the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis I mission focused on testing the SLS rocket and Orion capsule in deep space
